correctness.rationale: In characteristic two the odd cubic degree in Euler's identity puts every common gradient zero on the cubic. Absence of projective gradient zeros is equivalent to the quadrics forming a regular sequence in the surface and plane rings. The quotient Hilbert series is respectively (1+t)^4 and (1+t)^3, so the degree-five and degree-four multiplication maps are surjective exactly in the smooth cases; a common projective zero gives a nonzero evaluation quotient in those degrees. A separate exact implementation using adjacent swaps and elementary shears partitioned all 1,048,575 nonzero forms into 141 orbits, with 36 smooth orbits and 322,560 equations. It checked all 15 planes of each smooth representative and recovered each row of the table and the h=0 iff 13 or 15 points characterization. The exceptional orbit sizes are 28 and 1,680. For minimality choose a transverse section of the rational plane; for a smooth quadric the polar form is nondegenerate (a radical of dimension ≥2 would contain a geometric isotropic vector). A rational vector of norm 1 exists, since if the quadratic function were zero on all F2 vectors its polar form would vanish. Its polar perpendicular hyperplane cuts a conic whose one-dimensional polar radical has norm 1, so is geometrically smooth.
residual_risks: The independent replay uses an independently implemented copy of the rank criterion, not the frozen package's reported supplemental Gröbner computation. The conclusion is restricted to geometric smoothness over the F2 projective embedding.

value.rationale: Rational geometric transversality at the smallest field is a natural quantitative finite-field Bertini invariant. The complete distribution specifies exactly how existence can fail, and the two minimal-degree exceptional orbits and point-count test provide reusable witnesses and a check on bounds. The value is the section incidence computation, not reproducing the already known list of 36 surfaces.
residual_risks: No broader finite-field bound or extension-field distribution is established.
